blocks.text: A home network connects the different devices in a house, so that computers, mobile phones and printers can communicate with each other and share the same Internet connection. The router is the main device in a home network. Setting up the network makes data sharing easy and fast, and proper configuration improves its speed and safety.

items: Router: connects all the devices in the network.
Modem: connects the home network to the Internet Service Provider.
Network devices: computers, laptops and mobile phones.
Network cables for wired connections; Wi-Fi signals for wireless devices.

blocks.caption: Wired and wireless connections
rows: Ethernet cables, directly to a router or switch
Radio signals; Wi-Fi is the most common technology in homes
Can be slower than wired in some cases
Needs encryption and a strong password
Devices cannot move freely because of the cables
Devices can move freely within range; easy to install and use

blocks.alt: A cloud labelled ISP joins a modem, which joins a router labelled default gateway with Wi-Fi waves above it. An Ethernet cable runs down from the router to a wired PC. Dashed Wi-Fi lines run from the router to a laptop and a phone. A dashed box labelled guest network (separate name) holds two phones for visitors, Internet only. A green box says: secure the router, change the admin password, use WPA2 or WPA3 (not WEP), set a strong Wi-Fi password, and give visitors the guest network.
blocks.caption: A home network with wired, wireless and guest connections (original diagram after 1.9 and 1.10).
blocks.long_description: The modem links the house to the ISP; the router shares that connection with every device, by cable or by Wi-Fi, and acts as the default gateway to the Internet.

blocks.prompt: Give one advantage of a wired connection and one advantage of a wireless connection.
blocks.explanation: Wired: higher speed, more stable and more secure. Wireless: no cables, so devices can move freely within range, and it is easy to install.

items: Home network: router (centre), modem (to the ISP), devices, cables or Wi-Fi.
Wired: faster, stable, more secure; wireless: free movement, easy setup.
